No formatter config in analysis_options.yaml. So why does dart format treat the tree file and its identical copy differently?

Wait... maybe the issue is dart format's version-detection: it checks the SDK constraint in pubspec.yaml near the file to pick the Tall/Original style? Dart 3.7+ has the new formatter with a language-version-based style switch (tall style vs original style). The style is chosen from the file's package language version. A file in /tmp isn't part of any package → default (tall style for new SDK). A file inside this package → language version from pubspec.yaml environment sdk constraint. If pubspec declares `sdk: ^3.0.0` < 3.7, the file's language version might be < 3.7 → ORIGINAL style formatting!

Hmm, but the tree file: formatted with which style? If pubspec.yaml says sdk >=3.6 or something, tree files format in original style. The /tmp copy formats in tall style. And the earlier diff showed NO difference between the tree file and the formatted /tmp copy for fah_runapp... wait, that contradicts.

Hmm no wait, let me recheck the earlier diff run: `diff bin/fah_runapp.dart /tmp/fmtcheck/orig_fah_runapp.dart` — empty. And now `dart format /tmp/runapp_copy.dart` → 0 changed. And `dart format bin/fah_runapp.dart` → 1 changed.

If the /tmp copy was formatted in TALL style and equals the tree file, then the tree file is tall-style-formatted. And dart format on the tree file says "changed" — meaning in-tree it applies ORIGINAL style (language version from pubspec). So the repo's pubspec.yaml must declare an SDK constraint < 3.7 (e.g. `sdk: ^3.5.0`), pinning all repo files to the ORIGINAL formatter style, while dart's default for non-package files is the new TALL style.

So the test in question: which style does the repo use? If the repo language version is <3.7 (original style), then the gate is `dart format` at that language version — and bin/fah_runapp.dart fails it. The /tmp copy check is irrelevant (tall style).

So the real question: what does the repo's format gate look like, and does bin/fah_runapp.dart + the two test files pass it at the repo's language version?

Let me check pubspec.yaml SDK constraint and what the actual format gate runs in CI.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1557
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1557
- **Title**: feat(1552): roles resolve customProviders entries by name
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1552-roles-custom-providers` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +775
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T20:46:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T21:42:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1552

## Summary

A roles chain entry naming a `customProviders:` entry (`provider: aiai`) now resolves exactly like the equivalent kind+baseUrl+apiKeyName spelling — the natural hand-written config stops silently degrading to a single model.

### Design (per the GOAL card invariants)

1. **Resolution order** — `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry`: catalog name/kind first (unchanged, `resolveCliProviderSpec(honorBuildFilter: true)`); on a miss, the custom registry leg: `_findCustomProvider` (case-insensitive name match) → `resolveCliProviderSpec(entry.apiType)` (the entry.spec resolution, honoring the same build filter every user-facing roles surface applies) → `_throughCustomEntry` defaults `baseUrl`/`apiKeyName` from the entry where the ref omits them. **Explicit ref fields always win.**
2. **No collision surface** — reserved-name rule (`isReservedCustomProviderName`) already bars custom entries from catalog names; the registry leg only ever answers what the catalog missed.
3. **gh-760 contract preserved** — a name known to NEITHER catalog nor registry skips with the same named reason and degrades via `UnknownProviderRoleException` exactly as today (newer-version configs keep working across skew).
4. **Key provenance unchanged** (issue #40) — the widened NAME resolution never changes key rules: entry pin → endpoint-scoped `FA_KEY_<HOST>` slot → spec env names, byte-identical to the kind+baseUrl form (REG-2 asserts the forms pick the same slot in all three key layouts).
5. **Boot visibility (AC4)** — the gh-760 roles-drop warning additionally surfaces in the notice stream: `AgentCliConfig.rolesDropNotice` (set by `bin/fah_runapp.dart` alongside the existing stderr line), printed in line mode (`_loadAgentContext`) and re-printed after the TUI banner (`_runTuiRepl` — the alternate screen wipes stderr, the same rule as the third-party-skills hint).

### Wiring

- CLI startup (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`): resolver + `collectRoleSecrets` receive `saved.customProviders`.
- App `AgentService`: `.withEnv` boot maps the live `ProviderRegistry` into `CustomProviderEntry`s (kind ?? openai; no keyName — app keys are session-memory); the `@visibleForTesting` constructor gains the same param so ITs can drive the identical construction.
- `collectRoleSecrets`/`roleKeyNames`/`_refNeedsEndpointSlot` mirror the registry leg so entry-pinned keyNames and endpoint-scoped slots ride the preload set + secrets snapshot (without this, a resolving chain entry would still skip as keyless).
- No config-schema change; existing valid configs without the new form resolve byte-identically (all new params are optional, defaults empty).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — UT-1 (test/model_roles/model_resolver_custom_providers_test.dart): registry resolution, kind+baseUrl equivalence, entry defaults (endpoint slot, entry pin), explicit-ref precedence, case-insensitive match. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

+## Roles × custom providers
+
+A `roles:` chain entry can name a saved `customProviders:` entry **by name** (issue #1552) — the natural hand-written config works instead of silently degrading to a single model:
+
+```yaml
+customProviders:
+  - name: aiai
+    apiType: openai          # the adapter dialect (catalog spec)
+    baseUrl: https://api.bycom.by/v1
+    modelId: glm-4.6
+    keyName: AIAI_API_KEY    # optional: the env/secure-store slot for the key
+
+roles:
+  default:
+    - provider: aiai         # names the entry above
+      model: glm-4.6
+```
+
+Rules:
+
+- **Kind-vs-name**: resolution order is catalog name, then adapter kind (`chatgpt-codex`), then the `customProviders:` registry. Registry entries can never be named after catalog providers (reserved names), so the two namespaces never shadow. An entry known to NEITHER catalog nor registry still skips + degrades exactly as before (the roles config falls back to the single model with one warning — which also prints in the TUI, not only stderr).
+- **Defaults**: the entry supplies `baseUrl` and `keyName` where the chain ref omits them; explicit ref fields always win.
+- **Key slots** (issue #40 precedence): a custom endpoint's key resolves
+  from the entry's pinned `keyName` first, then the endpoint-scoped
+  `FA_KEY_<HOST>` store slot (e.g. `FA_KEY_API_BYCOM_BY`) or its
+  `_2`/`_3`… rotation stack, and only then falls back to the adapter
+  dialect's catalog env names (`OPENAI_API_KEY` for an `openai` entry —
+  the last-resort fallback, shared with the dialect's default endpoint).
+  Export `AIAI_API_KEY=<key>` (or `/key set FA_KEY_API_BYCOM_BY <key>`)
+  and every chain entry referencing the entry resolves.
+

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1557
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1557
- **Title**: feat(1552): roles resolve customProviders entries by name
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1552-roles-custom-providers` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +775
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T20:46:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T21:42:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1552

## Summary

A roles chain entry naming a `customProviders:` entry (`provider: aiai`) now resolves exactly like the equivalent kind+baseUrl+apiKeyName spelling — the natural hand-written config stops silently degrading to a single model.

### Design (per the GOAL card invariants)

1. **Resolution order** — `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry`: catalog name/kind first (unchanged, `resolveCliProviderSpec(honorBuildFilter: true)`); on a miss, the custom registry leg: `_findCustomProvider` (case-insensitive name match) → `resolveCliProviderSpec(entry.apiType)` (the entry.spec resolution, honoring the same build filter every user-facing roles surface applies) → `_throughCustomEntry` defaults `baseUrl`/`apiKeyName` from the entry where the ref omits them. **Explicit ref fields always win.**
2. **No collision surface** — reserved-name rule (`isReservedCustomProviderName`) already bars custom entries from catalog names; the registry leg only ever answers what the catalog missed.
3. **gh-760 contract preserved** — a name known to NEITHER catalog nor registry skips with the same named reason and degrades via `UnknownProviderRoleException` exactly as today (newer-version configs keep working across skew).
4. **Key provenance unchanged** (issue #40) — the widened NAME resolution never changes key rules: entry pin → endpoint-scoped `FA_KEY_<HOST>` slot → spec env names, byte-identical to the kind+baseUrl form (REG-2 asserts the forms pick the same slot in all three key layouts).
5. **Boot visibility (AC4)** — the gh-760 roles-drop warning additionally surfaces in the notice stream: `AgentCliConfig.rolesDropNotice` (set by `bin/fah_runapp.dart` alongside the existing stderr line), printed in line mode (`_loadAgentContext`) and re-printed after the TUI banner (`_runTuiRepl` — the alternate screen wipes stderr, the same rule as the third-party-skills hint).

### Wiring

- CLI startup (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`): resolver + `collectRoleSecrets` receive `saved.customProviders`.
- App `AgentService`: `.withEnv` boot maps the live `ProviderRegistry` into `CustomProviderEntry`s (kind ?? openai; no keyName — app keys are session-memory); the `@visibleForTesting` constructor gains the same param so ITs can drive the identical construction.
- `collectRoleSecrets`/`roleKeyNames`/`_refNeedsEndpointSlot` mirror the registry leg so entry-pinned keyNames and endpoint-scoped slots ride the preload set + secrets snapshot (without this, a resolving chain entry would still skip as keyless).
- No config-schema change; existing valid configs without the new form resolve byte-identically (all new params are optional, defaults empty).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — UT-1 (test/model_roles/model_resolver_custom_providers_test.dart): registry resolution, kind+baseUrl equivalence, entry defaults (endpoint slot, entry pin), explicit-ref precedence, case-insensitive match. IT-1 (test/cli/roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart): the user's bycom fixture through the verbatim boot pipeline (secureKeyPreloadNames → preload → collectRoleSecrets → resolver) — all five roles resolve, no skip, for explicit-`apiKeyName`, entry-pin, and endpoint-slot key layouts.
- **AC2** — UT-2: catalog-name + adapter-kind entries resolve identically with a loaded registry (parity against the empty-registry resolver).
- **AC3** — UT-3: unknown-in-both keeps the skip + `UnknownProviderRoleException` degrade; known entries still carry the role past an unknown one.
- **AC4** — line-mode IT prints the configured drop notice through `FakeCliIO`; the TUI re-print mirrors the skills-hint pattern in `_runTuiRepl` (same library seam, no TUI harness in the suite — static, see verification note).
- **AC5** — docs/agents/providers.md «Roles × custom providers»: kind-vs-name rule, FA_KEY_<HOST> key-slot rule, worked yaml example.
- **REG-1** — flutter_app/test/compaction_host_wiring_test.dart UT-2 harness extended: the custom-name form (store providerKind naming a saved entry) resolves like kind+baseUrl on both hosts (`sameResolutionAs`).
- **REG-2** — key provenance: custom-name and kind+baseUrl forms pick the SAME key base in every layout (entry pin / endpoint slot / spec env fallback); entry pin wins over the endpoint slot.

## Verification disclosure (honest)

This lane runs on the shared Mac agent host where the dart VM is SIGKILLed at launch by a machine-level guard (the known fleet condition, exit 137 — confirmed twice this session):

- `dart pub get` in the fresh worktree → **exit 137, zero output**.
- `dart analyze lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart` → **exit 137, zero output**.

Per the lane contract each gate was attempted once, never retried in a loop. **No dart test/analyze output could be produced; the PR's own CI is the real gate.** What was done instead:

- Static 1:1 trace of every new test assertion against the implementation paths (resolution order, key-slot selection per layout, skip-reason text, promote-safe null handling).
- Two real bugs caught and fixed by that static pass before commit: an unseeded fake secure store in the IT helper (store-backed variants would have found nothing), and a nullable access without promotion in the five-role loop.
- All changed files re-read post-edit; all pre-existing callers of the touched functions (`collectRoleSecrets`, `roleKeyNames`, `secureKeyPreloadNames`, `ModelRolesResolver`) checked for signature compatibility — every new parameter is optional with an empty default.
- God-file ceiling respected (largest touched file 2485 lines < 2800); barrel untouched (no new public API surface — the new param/field live on already-exported types).

## Non-goals respected

Custom names in `models:` slots / `/model` resolution, endpoint-scoped key rules, and CLI wizard changes are untouched. The name-resolution shape (entry name → apiType spec → per-entry defaults) leaves room for #1554 to layer per-entry timeout overrides without moving this seam.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

+A `roles:` chain entry can name a saved `customProviders:` entry **by name** (issue #1552) — the natural hand-written config works instead of silently degrading to a single model:

+customProviders:
+  - name: aiai

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1557
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1557
- **Title**: feat(1552): roles resolve customProviders entries by name
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1552-roles-custom-providers` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +775
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T20:46:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T21:42:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1552

## Summary

A roles chain entry naming a `customProviders:` entry (`provider: aiai`) now resolves exactly like the equivalent kind+baseUrl+apiKeyName spelling — the natural hand-written config stops silently degrading to a single model.

### Design (per the GOAL card invariants)

1. **Resolution order** — `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry`: catalog name/kind first (unchanged, `resolveCliProviderSpec(honorBuildFilter: true)`); on a miss, the custom registry leg: `_findCustomProvider` (case-insensitive name match) → `resolveCliProviderSpec(entry.apiType)` (the entry.spec resolution, honoring the same build filter every user-facing roles surface applies) → `_throughCustomEntry` defaults `baseUrl`/`apiKeyName` from the entry where the ref omits them. **Explicit ref fields always win.**
2. **No collision surface** — reserved-name rule (`isReservedCustomProviderName`) already bars custom entries from catalog names; the registry leg only ever answers what the catalog missed.
3. **gh-760 contract preserved** — a name known to NEITHER catalog nor registry skips with the same named reason and degrades via `UnknownProviderRoleException` exactly as today (newer-version configs keep working across skew).
4. **Key provenance unchanged** (issue #40) — the widened NAME resolution never changes key rules: entry pin → endpoint-scoped `FA_KEY_<HOST>` slot → spec env names, byte-identical to the kind+baseUrl form (REG-2 asserts the forms pick the same slot in all three key layouts).
5. **Boot visibility (AC4)** — the gh-760 roles-drop warning additionally surfaces in the notice stream: `AgentCliConfig.rolesDropNotice` (set by `bin/fah_runapp.dart` alongside the existing stderr line), printed in line mode (`_loadAgentContext`) and re-printed after the TUI banner (`_runTuiRepl` — the alternate screen wipes stderr, the same rule as the third-party-skills hint).

### Wiring

- CLI startup (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`): resolver + `collectRoleSecrets` receive `saved.customProviders`.
- App `AgentService`: `.withEnv` boot maps the live `ProviderRegistry` into `CustomProviderEntry`s (kind ?? openai; no keyName — app keys are session-memory); the `@visibleForTesting` constructor gains the same param so ITs can drive the identical construction.
- `collectRoleSecrets`/`roleKeyNames`/`_refNeedsEndpointSlot` mirror the registry leg so entry-pinned keyNames and endpoint-scoped slots ride the preload set + secrets snapshot (without this, a resolving chain entry would still skip as keyless).
- No config-schema change; existing valid configs without the new form resolve byte-identically (all new params are optional, defaults empty).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — UT-1 (test/model_roles/model_resolver_custom_providers_test.dart): registry resolution, kind+baseUrl equivalence, entry defaults (endpoint slot, entry pin), explicit-ref precedence, case-insensitive match. IT-1 (test/cli/roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart): the user's bycom fixture through the verbatim boot pipeline (secureKeyPreloadNames → preload → collectRoleSecrets → resolver) — all five roles resolve, no skip, for explicit-`apiKeyName`, entry-pin, and endpoint-slot key layouts.
- **AC2** — UT-2: catalog-name + adapter-kind entries resolve identically with a loaded registry (parity against the empty-registry resolver).
- **AC3** — UT-3: unknown-in-both keeps the skip + `UnknownProviderRoleException` degrade; known entries still carry the role past an unknown one.
- **AC4** — line-mode IT prints the configured drop notice through `FakeCliIO`; the TUI re-print mirrors the skills-hint pattern in `_runTuiRepl` (same library seam, no TUI harness in the suite — static, see verification note).
- **AC5** — docs/agents/providers.md «Roles × custom providers»: kind-vs-name rule, FA_KEY_<HOST> key-slot rule, worked yaml example.
- **REG-1** — flutter_app/test/compaction_host_wiring_test.dart UT-2 harness extended: the custom-name form (store providerKind naming a saved entry) resolves like kind+baseUrl on both hosts (`sameResolutionAs`).
- **REG-2** — key provenance: custom-name and kind+baseUrl forms pick the SAME key base in every layout (entry pin / endpoint slot / spec env fallback); entry pin wins over the endpoint slot.

## Verification disclosure (honest)

This lane runs on the shared Mac agent host where the dart VM is SIGKILLed at launch by a machine-level guard (the known fleet condition, exit 137 — confirmed twice this session):

- `dart pub get` in the fresh worktree → **exit 137, zero output**.
- `dart analyze lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart` → **exit 137, zero output**.

Per the lane contract each gate was attempted once, never retried in a loop. **No dart test/analyze output could be produced; the PR's own CI is the real gate.** What was done instead:

- Static 1:1 trace of every new test assertion against the implementation paths (resolution order, key-slot selection per layout, skip-reason text, promote-safe null handling).
- Two real bugs caught and fixed by that static pass before commit: an unseeded fake secure store in the IT helper (store-backed variants would have found nothing), and a nullable access without promotion in the five-role loop.
- All changed files re-read post-edit; all pre-existing callers of the touched functions (`collectRoleSecrets`, `roleKeyNames`, `secureKeyPreloadNames`, `ModelRolesResolver`) checked for signature compatibility — every new parameter is optional with an empty default.
- God-file ceiling respected (largest touched file 2485 lines < 2800); barrel untouched (no new public API surface — the new param/field live on already-exported types).

## Non-goals respected

Custom names in `models:` slots / `/model` resolution, endpoint-scoped key rules, and CLI wizard changes are untouched. The name-resolution shape (entry name → apiType spec → per-entry defaults) leaves room for #1554 to layer per-entry timeout overrides without moving this seam.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

**Error**: `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart:245:41 — Property 'kind' cannot be accessed on 'ProviderSpec?' because it is potentially null`.

**Root cause**: the #1552 registry leg changed `spec` from a `final` (promote-on-check) to a reassigned `var` (catalog miss → registry-leg reassignment). `spec` is captured by the `buildRouted` closure, and Dart flow analysis never promotes a captured local that is assigned more than once — so the `if (spec == null) return null;` guard stopped covering the `spec.kind` read inside the closure.

**Fix**: bind `final resolvedSpec = spec;` immediately after the early null return (null only ever falls through to the registry leg, then the gh-760 degrade path — exactly the intended semantic) and read the alias in all four downstream uses (`_keyBaseName`, `_missingKeyHint`, `_streamFactory(resolvedSpec.kind)`, `buildCatalogModel(resolvedSpec.name)`). +9/−4, no behavior change.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1557
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1557
- **Title**: feat(1552): roles resolve customProviders entries by name
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1552-roles-custom-providers` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +775
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T20:46:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T21:42:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1552

## Summary

A roles chain entry naming a `customProviders:` entry (`provider: aiai`) now resolves exactly like the equivalent kind+baseUrl+apiKeyName spelling — the natural hand-written config stops silently degrading to a single model.

### Design (per the GOAL card invariants)

1. **Resolution order** — `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry`: catalog name/kind first (unchanged, `resolveCliProviderSpec(honorBuildFilter: true)`); on a miss, the custom registry leg: `_findCustomProvider` (case-insensitive name match) → `resolveCliProviderSpec(entry.apiType)` (the entry.spec resolution, honoring the same build filter every user-facing roles surface applies) → `_throughCustomEntry` defaults `baseUrl`/`apiKeyName` from the entry where the ref omits them. **Explicit ref fields always win.**
2. **No collision surface** — reserved-name rule (`isReservedCustomProviderName`) already bars custom entries from catalog names; the registry leg only ever answers what the catalog missed.
3. **gh-760 contract preserved** — a name known to NEITHER catalog nor registry skips with the same named reason and degrades via `UnknownProviderRoleException` exactly as today (newer-version configs keep working across skew).
4. **Key provenance unchanged** (issue #40) — the widened NAME resolution never changes key rules: entry pin → endpoint-scoped `FA_KEY_<HOST>` slot → spec env names, byte-identical to the kind+baseUrl form (REG-2 asserts the forms pick the same slot in all three key layouts).
5. **Boot visibility (AC4)** — the gh-760 roles-drop warning additionally surfaces in the notice stream: `AgentCliConfig.rolesDropNotice` (set by `bin/fah_runapp.dart` alongside the existing stderr line), printed in line mode (`_loadAgentContext`) and re-printed after the TUI banner (`_runTuiRepl` — the alternate screen wipes stderr, the same rule as the third-party-skills hint).

### Wiring

- CLI startup (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`): resolver + `collectRoleSecrets` receive `saved.customProviders`.
- App `AgentService`: `.withEnv` boot maps the live `ProviderRegistry` into `CustomProviderEntry`s (kind ?? openai; no keyName — app keys are session-memory); the `@visibleForTesting` constructor gains the same param so ITs can drive the identical construction.
- `collectRoleSecrets`/`roleKeyNames`/`_refNeedsEndpointSlot` mirror the registry leg so entry-pinned keyNames and endpoint-scoped slots ride the preload set + secrets snapshot (without this, a resolving chain entry would still skip as keyless).
- No config-schema change; existing valid configs without the new form resolve byte-identically (all new params are optional, defaults empty).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — UT-1 (test/model_roles/model_resolver_custom_providers_test.dart): registry resolution, kind+baseUrl equivalence, entry defaults (endpoint slot, entry pin), explicit-ref precedence, case-insensitive match. IT-1 (test/cli/roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart): the user's bycom fixture through the verbatim boot pipeline (secureKeyPreloadNames → preload → collectRoleSecrets → resolver) — all five roles resolve, no skip, for explicit-`apiKeyName`, entry-pin, and endpoint-slot key layouts.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

+## Roles × custom providers
+
+A `roles:` chain entry can name a saved `customProviders:` entry **by name** (issue #1552) — the natural hand-written config works instead of silently degrading to a single model:
+
+```yaml
+customProviders:
+  - name: aiai
+    apiType: openai          # the adapter dialect (catalog spec)
+    baseUrl: https://api.bycom.by/v1
+    modelId: glm-4.6
+    keyName: AIAI_API_KEY    # optional: the env/secure-store slot for the key
+
+roles:
+  default:
+    - provider: aiai         # names the entry above
+      model: glm-4.6
+```
+
+Rules:
+
+- **Kind-vs-name**: resolution order is catalog name, then adapter kind (`chatgpt-codex`), then the `customProviders:` registry. Registry entries can never be named after catalog providers (reserved names), so the two namespaces never shadow. An entry known to NEITHER catalog nor registry still skips + degrades exactly as before (the roles config falls back to the single model with one warning — which also prints in the TUI, not only stderr).
+- **Defaults**: the entry supplies `baseUrl` and `keyName` where the chain ref omits them; explicit ref fields always win.
+- **Key slots** (issue #40 precedence): a custom endpoint's key resolves
+  from the entry's pinned `keyName` first, then the endpoint-scoped
+  `FA_KEY_<HOST>` store slot (e.g. `FA_KEY_API_BYCOM_BY`) or its
+  `_2`/`_3`… rotation stack, and only then falls back to the adapter
+  dialect's catalog env names (`OPENAI_API_KEY` for an `openai` entry —
+  the last-resort fallback, shared with the dialect's default endpoint).
+  Export `AIAI_API_KEY=<key>` (or `/key set FA_KEY_API_BYCOM_BY <key>`)
+  and every chain entry referencing the entry resolves.

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done

          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'

          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.

            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1557
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1557
- **Title**: feat(1552): roles resolve customProviders entries by name
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1552-roles-custom-providers` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +775
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T20:46:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T21:42:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1552

## Summary

A roles chain entry naming a `customProviders:` entry (`provider: aiai`) now resolves exactly like the equivalent kind+baseUrl+apiKeyName spelling — the natural hand-written config stops silently degrading to a single model.

### Design (per the GOAL card invariants)

1. **Resolution order** — `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry`: catalog name/kind first (unchanged, `resolveCliProviderSpec(honorBuildFilter: true)`); on a miss, the custom registry leg: `_findCustomProvider` (case-insensitive name match) → `resolveCliProviderSpec(entry.apiType)` (the entry.spec resolution, honoring the same build filter every user-facing roles surface applies) → `_throughCustomEntry` defaults `baseUrl`/`apiKeyName` from the entry where the ref omits them. **Explicit ref fields always win.**
2. **No collision surface** — reserved-name rule (`isReservedCustomProviderName`) already bars custom entries from catalog names; the registry leg only ever answers what the catalog missed.
3. **gh-760 contract preserved** — a name known to NEITHER catalog nor registry skips with the same named reason and degrades via `UnknownProviderRoleException` exactly as today (newer-version configs keep working across skew).
4. **Key provenance unchanged** (issue #40) — the widened NAME resolution never changes key rules: entry pin → endpoint-scoped `FA_KEY_<HOST>` slot → spec env names, byte-identical to the kind+baseUrl form (REG-2 asserts the forms pick the same slot in all three key layouts).
5. **Boot visibility (AC4)** — the gh-760 roles-drop warning additionally surfaces in the notice stream: `AgentCliConfig.rolesDropNotice` (set by `bin/fah_runapp.dart` alongside the existing stderr line), printed in line mode (`_loadAgentContext`) and re-printed after the TUI banner (`_runTuiRepl` — the alternate screen wipes stderr, the same rule as the third-party-skills hint).

### Wiring

- CLI startup (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`): resolver + `collectRoleSecrets` receive `saved.customProviders`.
- App `AgentService`: `.withEnv` boot maps the live `ProviderRegistry` into `CustomProviderEntry`s (kind ?? openai; no keyName — app keys are session-memory); the `@visibleForTesting` constructor gains the same param so ITs can drive the identical construction.
- `collectRoleSecrets`/`roleKeyNames`/`_refNeedsEndpointSlot` mirror the registry leg so entry-pinned keyNames and endpoint-scoped slots ride the preload set + secrets snapshot (without this, a resolving chain entry would still skip as keyless).
- No config-schema change; existing valid configs without the new form resolve byte-identically (all new params are optional, defaults empty).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — UT-1 (test/model_roles/model_resolver_custom_providers_test.dart): registry resolution, kind+baseUrl equivalence, entry defaults (endpoint slot, entry pin), explicit-ref precedence, case-insensitive match. IT-1 (test/cli/roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart): the user's bycom fixture through the verbatim boot pipeline (secureKeyPreloadNames → preload → collectRoleSecrets → resolver) — all five roles resolve, no skip, for explicit-`apiKeyName`, entry-pin, and endpoint-slot key layouts.
- **AC2** — UT-2: catalog-name + adapter-kind entries resolve identically with a loaded registry (parity against the empty-registry resolver).
- **AC3** — UT-3: unknown-in-both keeps the skip + `UnknownProviderRoleException` degrade; known entries still carry the role past an unknown one.
- **AC4** — line-mode IT prints the configured drop notice through `FakeCliIO`; the TUI re-print mirrors the skills-hint pattern in `_runTuiRepl` (same library seam, no TUI harness in the suite — static, see verification note).
- **AC5** — docs/agents/providers.md «Roles × custom providers»: kind-vs-name rule, FA_KEY_<HOST> key-slot rule, worked yaml example.
- **REG-1** — flutter_app/test/compaction_host_wiring_test.dart UT-2 harness extended: the custom-name form (store providerKind naming a saved entry) resolves like kind+baseUrl on both hosts (`sameResolutionAs`).
- **REG-2** — key provenance: custom-name and kind+baseUrl forms pick the SAME key base in every layout (entry pin / endpoint slot / spec env fallback); entry pin wins over the endpoint slot.

## Verification disclosure (honest)

This lane runs on the shared Mac agent host where the dart VM is SIGKILLed at launch by a machine-level guard (the known fleet condition, exit 137 — confirmed twice this session):

- `dart pub get` in the fresh worktree → **exit 137, zero output**.
- `dart analyze lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart` → **exit 137, zero output**.

Per the lane contract each gate was attempted once, never retried in a loop. **No dart test/analyze output could be produced; the PR's own CI is the real gate.** What was done instead:

- Static 1:1 trace of every new test assertion against the implementation paths (resolution order, key-slot selection per layout, skip-reason text, promote-safe null handling).
- Two real bugs caught and fixed by that static pass before commit: an unseeded fake secure store in the IT helper (store-backed variants would have found nothing), and a nullable access without promotion in the five-role loop.
- All changed files re-read post-edit; all pre-existing callers of the touched functions (`collectRoleSecrets`, `roleKeyNames`, `secureKeyPreloadNames`, `ModelRolesResolver`) checked for signature compatibility — every new parameter is optional with an empty default.
- God-file ceiling respected (largest touched file 2485 lines < 2800); barrel untouched (no new public API surface — the new param/field live on already-exported types).

## Non-goals respected

Custom names in `models:` slots / `/model` resolution, endpoint-scoped key rules, and CLI wizard changes are untouched. The name-resolution shape (entry name → apiType spec → per-entry defaults) leaves room for #1554 to layer per-entry timeout overrides without moving this seam.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

**Error**: `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart:245:41 — Property 'kind' cannot be accessed on 'ProviderSpec?' because it is potentially null`.

**Root cause**: the #1552 registry leg changed `spec` from a `final` (promote-on-check) to a reassigned `var` (catalog miss → registry-leg reassignment). `spec` is captured by the `buildRouted` closure, and Dart flow analysis never promotes a captured local that is assigned more than once — so the `if (spec == null) return null;` guard stopped covering the `spec.kind` read inside the closure.

**Fix**: bind `final resolvedSpec = spec;` immediately after the early null return (null only ever falls through to the registry leg, then the gh-760 degrade path — exactly the intended semantic) and read the alias in all four downstream uses (`_keyBaseName`, `_missingKeyHint`, `_streamFactory(resolvedSpec.kind)`, `buildCatalogModel(resolvedSpec.name)`). +9/−4, no behavior change.

**Same-class audit over the whole PR diff**: the only other reassigned-nullable-spec read is `startup.dart` `_refNeedsEndpointSlot` (`return spec != null && !sameEndpoint(baseUrl, spec.defaultBaseUrl)`) — that local is NOT captured by any closure, so the inline guard promotes legally. All other nullable values introduced by this PR (`entry`, `resolved`, registry fields) are if-null- or bang-guarded; no other member reads on possibly-null specs exist.

blocks.text:
# gh-1059 AC4: the real-keychain runner guard — `security`
      # add/find/delete against the runner's login keychain through the
      # bounded-helper machinery (outcome classification incl. stderr
      # tails, env merge, timeout kill). The group is tagged `integration`
      # (real side effects), so the Linux core shards and the pre-commit
      # gate skip it; this macOS leg is where it actually executes. Skips
      # with a named reason when no `security` binary / default keychain.
      - name: dart test secure key store (macOS Keychain live legs)
        run: dart test test/secrets/secure_key_store_test.dart --tags integration

  static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1538: the publish dry-run below rehearses the tag-stamped
          # stage (gh-1522), moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — tag math needs the full tag graph
          # (blobless per gh-1477, same incantation that leg used).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1557
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1557
- **Title**: feat(1552): roles resolve customProviders entries by name
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1552-roles-custom-providers` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +775
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T20:46:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T21:42:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1552

## Summary

A roles chain entry naming a `customProviders:` entry (`provider: aiai`) now resolves exactly like the equivalent kind+baseUrl+apiKeyName spelling — the natural hand-written config stops silently degrading to a single model.

### Design (per the GOAL card invariants)

1. **Resolution order** — `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry`: catalog name/kind first (unchanged, `resolveCliProviderSpec(honorBuildFilter: true)`); on a miss, the custom registry leg: `_findCustomProvider` (case-insensitive name match) → `resolveCliProviderSpec(entry.apiType)` (the entry.spec resolution, honoring the same build filter every user-facing roles surface applies) → `_throughCustomEntry` defaults `baseUrl`/`apiKeyName` from the entry where the ref omits them. **Explicit ref fields always win.**
2. **No collision surface** — reserved-name rule (`isReservedCustomProviderName`) already bars custom entries from catalog names; the registry leg only ever answers what the catalog missed.
3. **gh-760 contract preserved** — a name known to NEITHER catalog nor registry skips with the same named reason and degrades via `UnknownProviderRoleException` exactly as today (newer-version configs keep working across skew).
4. **Key provenance unchanged** (issue #40) — the widened NAME resolution never changes key rules: entry pin → endpoint-scoped `FA_KEY_<HOST>` slot → spec env names, byte-identical to the kind+baseUrl form (REG-2 asserts the forms pick the same slot in all three key layouts).
5. **Boot visibility (AC4)** — the gh-760 roles-drop warning additionally surfaces in the notice stream: `AgentCliConfig.rolesDropNotice` (set by `bin/fah_runapp.dart` alongside the existing stderr line), printed in line mode (`_loadAgentContext`) and re-printed after the TUI banner (`_runTuiRepl` — the alternate screen wipes stderr, the same rule as the third-party-skills hint).

Custom names in `models:` slots / `/model` resolution, endpoint-scoped key rules, and CLI wizard changes are untouched. The name-resolution shape (entry name → apiType spec → per-entry defaults) leaves room for #1554 to layer per-entry timeout overrides without moving this seam.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
